artworks.title: Ulysses at the Court of Alcinous
artworks.description: Hayez seats the Phaeacian queen beside her husband as Odysseus weeps to Demodocus' song — Arete as the courtly presence Homer tells the stranger to clasp first.

artworks.title: Ulysses in the Palace of Alcinous
artworks.description: Lagrenée follows Nausicaa's counsel: Odysseus throws himself at the feet of Alcinous and Arete — the queen whose favour decides whether the stranger will be sent home.

artworks.title: Odysseus before Alcinous, King of the Phaeacians
artworks.description: Malmström's throne-room scene keeps Arete within the Phaeacian court that hears Odysseus — the wise queen of Scheria as the Odyssey's image of female authority at the world's edge.

popCulture.title: Arete (mythology)
popCulture.description: Alcinous' queen, whom Odysseus is told to clasp first, remains the Odyssey's image of wise female authority at the edge of the world.

films.title: Ulysses
films.description: Ludmilla Dudarova's Arete receives the shipwrecked stranger with Alcinous — Homer's counsel made flesh: clasp the queen first.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: Sally Plumb's Arete stands as Phaeacian queen beside Krabbé's Alcinous — the wise authority Nausicaa tells Odysseus to win.

music.title: Nausicaa
music.description: Glanville-Hicks' Athens premiere casts Arete as queen of Drepanum — Graves' Phaeacian mother in the opera that makes Nausicaa the Odyssey's author.
